title: Champurrado: Thick Mexican Chocolate and Masa Drink
summary: Masa harina is toasted and blended with warm water, then simmered with milk, Mexican chocolate, piloncillo, cinnamon and star anise until thick and frothy.

ingredients.item: Mexican table chocolate (such as Abuelita or Ibarra), chopped
piloncillo, grated, or dark brown sugar
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Toast the masa
steps.text: Toast the masa harina in the dry saucepan over medium heat, stirring constantly, for about 3 minutes until fragrant and pale golden. Tip into the blender or a bowl and cool for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Make a slurry
steps.text: Add the warm water and blend, or whisk hard, until completely smooth with no lumps.

steps.title: Melt the chocolate
steps.text: In the same saucepan, combine the milk, chocolate, piloncillo, salt, cinnamon and star anise. Heat over medium heat, whisking, for about 5 minutes until the chocolate melts and the sugar dissolves.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Pour in the masa mixture, whisking. Bring to a gentle boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 8-10 minutes, whisking often and scraping the bottom so it doesn't catch, until it coats a spoon like thick custard.

steps.title: Froth and serve
steps.text: Remove the cinnamon and star anise, whisk until frothy (with a molinillo if you have one) and ladle into mugs while hot.

tips: Whisk constantly once the masa goes in; it sticks to the pan easily.
Mexican chocolate is grainy and already sweet and spiced, so taste before adding more sugar.
If you can't find piloncillo, dark brown sugar gives a similar molasses flavour.
Champurrado thickens as it stands; loosen with a splash of hot milk.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers, covered, for up to 2 days. Reheat gently, whisking in a little milk. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
